title: Why Is the U.S. Building the Saudi Nuclear Program While Destroying Iran’s?

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重新构想者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you, and you turned a DJ booth
sentences.zh: 回想当年我在黑胶唱片时代的夜店当DJ时，每晚你都要带着300件你最珍视的传家宝去工作，你把DJ台

sentences.en: into this living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 变成了一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，里面摆满了精美的50年前的古董。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重新构想者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times,
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，

sentences.en: I'm Rachel Abrams, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是雷切尔·艾布拉姆斯，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, the United States signed a historic deal that allows Saudi Arabia to develop a nuclear program, even as the Trump administration escalates a war against Iran
sentences.zh: 周三，美国签署了一项具有历史意义的协议，允许沙特阿拉伯发展核计划，尽管与此同时，特朗普政府正在升级针对伊朗的战争，

sentences.en: that the White House says is about destroying its nuclear capabilities.
sentences.zh: 白宫称这场战争旨在摧毁伊朗的核能力。

sentences.en: Today, David Sanger explains what Saudi Arabia and the U.S.
sentences.zh: 今天，大卫·桑格将解释沙特阿拉伯和美国

sentences.en: are each getting out of the deal and why its prompted worries about nuclear proliferation across a region that is already engulfed in an escalating war.
sentences.zh: 在这项协议中各自获得了什么，以及为什么它引发了人们对核扩散的担忧，而此时该地区已经陷入不断升级的战争之中。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, July 23rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月23日，星期四。

sentences.en: So, David, when I saw this news about this Saudi nuclear deal, I will confess I was surprised.
sentences.zh: 大卫，当我看到关于沙特核协议的这个消息时，我必须承认我很惊讶。

sentences.en: I had a bunch of questions, but I assume that you, longtime Washington correspondent, nuclear expert, were probably not quite as surprised as I was.
sentences.zh: 我有一连串的问题，但我猜你作为资深的华盛顿记者和核专家，可能不像我那么惊讶吧？

sentences.en: Not surprised because this has been brewing for a long time.
sentences.zh: 并不惊讶，因为这已经酝酿了很长时间。

sentences.en: More than 10 years, actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上已经超过10年了。

sentences.en: But it has taken many different forMs.
sentences.zh: 但它采取过许多不同的形式。

sentences.en: For a while, the Biden administration wanted to make this part of a much broader deal with Saudi Arabia about recognizing Israel.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，拜登政府希望将其作为与沙特阿拉伯关于承认以色列的更广泛协议的一部分。

sentences.en: The Trump administration has dealt with it more as a business deal, but we knew it was coming.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府更多地把它当作一桩商业交易来处理，但我们知道它迟早会来。

sentences.en: The question is, what were the terms?
sentences.zh: 问题是，具体条款是什么？

sentences.en: So, let's actually talk about that next.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们接下来就来谈谈这个。

sentences.en: What do we know so far about what is included in this deal?
sentences.zh: 关于这项协议包含的内容，我们目前了解多少？

sentences.en: Well, the core of it is that Saudi Arabia gets to build at least two nuclear reactors, probably more, that this will last for three decades, and that the business
sentences.zh: 嗯，它的核心是沙特阿拉伯可以建造至少两个核反应堆，可能还会更多，这将持续三十年，而且这笔生意

sentences.en: will largely go to American companies, which is to say Westinghouse, which even though it has significant Canadian ownership these days, is still a big jobs provider in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 将主要流向美国公司，也就是西屋公司。尽管它现在拥有大量加拿大股权，但它仍然是美国的一个大型就业岗位提供者。

sentences.en: So, what the United States gets out of it is an extension of the president's determination to export American goods and to make sure that American allies
sentences.zh: 因此，美国从中得到的是总统决心的延伸，即出口美国商品，并确保美国的盟友

sentences.en: are tied to American energy systeMs.
sentences.zh: 与美国的能源系统绑定在一起。

sentences.en: But there's a catch, as there always is with things nuclear, and that has to do with the question of who makes Saudi Arabia's fuel and what kind of inspections the Saudis agree to.
sentences.zh: 但这里有个陷阱，核问题向来如此，这与谁来为沙特阿拉伯制造燃料以及沙特人同意接受什么样的视察有关。

sentences.en: And just to be clear, David, it sounds like from what you're describing that this is a civilian energy program, right?
sentences.zh: 大卫，为了明确起见，从你描述的情况来看，这是一个民用能源计划，对吧？

sentences.en: It's entirely a civilian energy program, which means that its intent is to help Saudi Arabia build nuclear power plants the way many other advanced economies have,
sentences.zh: 这完全是一个民用能源计划，这意味着其意图是帮助沙特阿拉伯像许多其他先进经济体一样建造核电站，

sentences.en: including many countries that don't have nuclear weapons.
sentences.zh: 包括许多没有核武器的国家。

sentences.en: Think about Japan or Germany or South Korea.
sentences.zh: 想想日本、德国或韩国。

sentences.en: But the critical problem comes in the supply of nuclear fuel.
sentences.zh: 但关键的问题出在核燃料的供应上。

sentences.en: If you are making your own nuclear fuel and enriching uranium up to, say, 3%, well, that's fine.
sentences.zh: 如果你在制造自己的核燃料并将铀浓缩到比如3%的水平，那没问题。

sentences.en: That's the level at which you can use that uranium as a source for your nuclear electricity generation.
sentences.zh: 那是你可以将铀用作核电发电来源的水平。

sentences.en: But if you keep enriching up to 90%, suddenly you have the makings of an atomic bomb.
sentences.zh: 但如果你继续浓缩到90%，你突然就具备了制造原子弹的原料。

sentences.en: And so the whole effort from the 1950s forward, from Eisenhower's Atoms for Peace program to spread nuclear technology around the world
sentences.zh: 因此，从20世纪50年代以来，从艾森豪威尔的“和平原子”计划向全球传播核技术

sentences.en: and make cheap nuclear energy available to all, has been to find a way to let countries produce nuclear energy without getting the stuff they need
sentences.zh: 并让所有人都能获得廉价核能的整个努力，一直都是在寻找一种方法，让国家能够生产核能量，而又不会获得那些需要

sentences.en: to divert to a nuclear weapons program.
sentences.zh: 被挪用到核武器计划中的物质。

sentences.en: Just so I'm clear, David, this deal is about providing Saudi Arabia with fuel, right?
sentences.zh: 为了确保我没听错，大卫，这项协议是关于向沙特阿拉伯提供燃料的，对吧？

sentences.en: Not letting them enrich their own fuel, which would avoid the threat that you just explained.
sentences.zh: 而不是让他们浓缩自己的燃料，这样就能避免你刚刚解释的威胁。

sentences.en: Well, Rachel, that's where this deal gets very vague.
sentences.zh: 嗯，雷切尔，这就是这项协议变得非常模糊的地方。

sentences.en: It allows the Saudis to purchase the nuclear reactors, which will take years to build.
sentences.zh: 它允许沙特购买核反应堆，而这需要数年时间才能建成。

sentences.en: But it doesn't resolve the question of whether they are making their own fuel or whether they are buying it from someone else, including the United States.
sentences.zh: 但它并没有解决这样一个问题：他们是自己制造燃料，还是从包括美国在内的其他人那里购买。

sentences.en: Instead, it refers that to a committee to go study the question of whether or not it even makes economic sense for Saudi Arabia to make its own fuel.
sentences.zh: 相反，它将这个问题交由一个委员会去研究，以探讨沙特阿拉伯自己制造燃料在经济上是否说得通。

sentences.en: It sort of kicks that can down the road, it sounds like, on this important question.
sentences.zh: 听起来，它在这个重要问题上把皮球踢到了以后。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Okay, I want to back up just for a second, though, David, because you had said just a couple minutes ago that this deal had been in the works for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 好吧，大卫，我想稍微倒退一下，因为你几分钟前说过，这项协议已经筹备了很长时间。

sentences.en: So I want to talk about the origin of all of this.
sentences.zh: 所以我想要讨论这一切的起源。

sentences.en: Like, when and why did these talks begin in the first place?
sentences.zh: 比如，这些会谈最初是在什么时候、为什么开始的？

sentences.en: Well, Saudi Arabia wanted a deal for the same reason all of its Arab neighbors want deals.
sentences.zh: 嗯，沙特阿拉伯想要达成协议，原因和它所有阿拉伯邻国想要协议的原因一样。

sentences.en: They all want nuclear power.
sentences.zh: 他们都想要核电。

sentences.en: They're thinking about a future in which their economies are driven as much by data centers as petroleum.
sentences.zh: 他们在考虑这样一个未来：他们的经济将同样受到数据中心和石油的驱动。

sentences.en: They want to build modern societies.
sentences.zh: 他们想要建设现代社会。

sentences.en: They're conscious to some degree of the environmental effects.
sentences.zh: 他们在某种程度上意识到了环境的影响。

sentences.en: And so you've seen many countries in the region turn to nuclear energy.
sentences.zh: 所以你会看到该地区的许多国家转向核能。

sentences.en: One of Saudi Arabia's most prosperous neighbors, the United Arab Emirates, decided back 20 years ago they wanted nuclear power plants.
sentences.zh: 沙特阿拉伯最繁荣的邻国之一——阿拉伯联合酋长国，在20年前就决定他们想要核电站。

sentences.en: And they struck a deal with the United States in 2009.
sentences.zh: 他们在2009年与美国达成了一项协议。

sentences.en: And today they have four nuclear power plants that are up and running.
sentences.zh: 今天他们有四座正在运营的核电站。

sentences.en: But to do that, they had to go reach a deal with the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但要做到这一点，他们必须与美国达成一项协议，

sentences.en: that every country that's using nuclear technology of American origin has to go strike.
sentences.zh: 每一个使用美源核技术的国家都必须达成这项协议。

sentences.en: And that is what's called a 1-2-3 agreement.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的123协议。

sentences.en: Sounds strange.
sentences.zh: 听起来很奇怪。

sentences.en: It comes out of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954.
sentences.zh: 它源自1954年的《原子能法》。

sentences.en: What it means, essentially, is if you are going to buy U.S.
sentences.zh: 从本质上讲，这意味着如果你要购买美国的

sentences.en: technology, you have to agree to some U.S.
sentences.zh: 技术，你就必须同意一些美国的

sentences.en: restrictions.
sentences.zh: 限制。

sentences.en: When the UAE negotiated its deal in 2009, it was considered probably the gold standard of these kinds of arrangements because the UAE agreed
sentences.zh: 当阿联酋在2009年谈判其协议时，它被认为是这类安排的黄金标准，因为阿联酋同意

sentences.en: that it would not produce its own nuclear fuel and that it would allow international inspectors for the most intrusive kind of inspections.
sentences.zh: 它不会生产自己的核燃料，并将允许国际核查人员进行最具侵入性的视察。

sentences.en: And so the thought was,
sentences.zh: 所以当时的设想是，

sentences.en: OK, we've set this standard.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们已经设定了这个标准。

sentences.en: Let's apply this to other countries.
sentences.zh: 让我们把它应用到其他国家。

sentences.en: And when the Saudis began discussing this with some of President Trump's closest allies during the first term, it was clear that they were more reluctant than the UAE
sentences.zh: 当沙特人在特朗普总统第一任期内开始与特朗普的一些最亲密盟友讨论这个问题时，很明显，他们比阿联酋更不愿

sentences.en: to give up their right to produce nuclear fuel and to allow those intrusive inspections.
sentences.zh: 放弃生产核燃料的权利以及允许这些侵入性视察。

sentences.en: So if those talks started in the first Trump administration, what has happened since then?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果这些会谈始于第一届特朗普政府，自那以后发生了什么？

sentences.en: Why did this deal only come about now?
sentences.zh: 为什么这项协议直到现在才达成？

sentences.en: Well, the Biden administration picked it up and President Biden wanted to make a nuclear deal part of a larger political arrangement with Saudi Arabia that would include
sentences.zh: 嗯，拜登政府接手了此事，拜登总统希望将核协议作为与沙特阿拉伯更大政治安排的一部分，其中包括

sentences.en: Saudi diplomatic recognition of Israel.
sentences.zh: 沙特对以色列的外交承认。

sentences.en: And so the nuclear deal was a sweetener for that.
sentences.zh: 所以核协议是其中的一个甜头。

sentences.en: And they were all linked together.
sentences.zh: 它们是环环相扣的。

sentences.en: The Saudis also were demanding that Israel allow a Palestinian state to exiSt.
sentences.zh: 沙特人还要求以色列允许巴勒斯坦国存在。

sentences.en: So there were these negotiations that were all wrapped into one big ball and they were getting very close to completion when the terror attacks of October 7, 2023 happened.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些谈判被包裹成一个大杂烩，眼看就要完成时，2023年10月7日的恐怖袭击发生了。

sentences.en: And that blew up the entire thing.
sentences.zh: 这彻底炸毁了整件事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of people will remember that when Israel started retaliating for that October 7 attack by bombing Gaza, the idea that Saudi Arabia
sentences.zh: 我想很多人都会记得，当以色列开始对10月7日的袭击进行轰炸加沙的报复时，沙特阿拉伯

sentences.en: would normalize diplomatic relations with Israel, that was a total non-starter at that moment.
sentences.zh: 将与以色列实现外交关系正常化的想法，在当时完全是不可能的。

sentences.en: That's absolutely right, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 完全正确，雷切尔。

sentences.en: And beyond that, we now have some evidence that Hamas timed their attack on Israel in part to blow up the deal with the Saudis.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，我们现在有一些证据表明，哈马斯选择在那个时间点发动对以色列的袭击，部分原因就是为了炸毁与沙特的协议。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So when President Trump came in, he recognized he was going to have to decouple the nuclear deal from the diplomatic arrangement because the Saudis aren't going to recognize
sentences.zh: 因此，当特朗普总统上台时，他认识到他必须将核协议与外交安排脱钩，因为沙特人根本不会在外交上承认

sentences.en: Israel diplomatically for years if they can ever pull that off.
sentences.zh: 以色列，如果他们未来真能做到这一点的话。

sentences.en: And Mohammed bin Salman, known as MBS in the region, the Saudi leader, made clear to President Trump last fall that diplomatic recognition of Israel
sentences.zh: 穆罕默德·本·萨尔曼（在地区被称为MBS），这位沙特领导人，去年秋天向特朗普总统明确表示，外交承认以色列

sentences.en: was pretty low on his priority liSt.
sentences.zh: 在他的优先事项名单上排得很靠后。

sentences.en: But the nuclear deal was high on his priority liSt.
sentences.zh: 但核协议在他的优先事项名单上排得很靠前。

sentences.en: And because it has the promise of bringing billions of dollars of revenue to the United States, it's high on President Trump's list as well.
sentences.zh: 而且由于它有望为美国带来数十亿美元的收入，它在特朗普总统的名单上也排得很靠前。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Basically, the United States is thinking
sentences.zh: 基本上，美国现在的想法是：

sentences.en: Israel normalization, not as high on the list as all the money we could get from this deal, hence why we might cut a deal with Saudi Arabia that has these kind of favorable,
sentences.zh: 以色列正常化，在名单上的重要性不如我们从这笔交易中能得到的所有金钱，因此我们可能会与沙特阿拉伯达成一项具有这种有利的、

sentences.en: looser restrictions.
sentences.zh: 更宽松限制的协议。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the question was, how loose would those restrictions be?
sentences.zh: 问题是，这些限制会有多宽松？

sentences.en: Now, to be fair to President Trump, when the Biden administration was negotiating before October 7th, they were moving towards some pretty loose restrictions themselves.
sentences.zh: 公平地说，对特朗普总统而言，当拜登政府在10月7日之前进行谈判时，他们自己也在向一些相当宽松的限制迈进。

sentences.en: So it's not clear to me that the terms would have been any tougher under President Biden.
sentences.zh: 所以我并不清楚在拜登总统领导下条款会不会更严厉。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But the Biden administration was going to get something very different and very significant in return, which was a Palestinian state and diplomatic relations with Israel
sentences.zh: 但拜登政府将换取非常不同且非常重大回报，那就是巴勒斯坦国的建立以及沙特阿拉伯与以色列建立

sentences.en: being established by Saudi Arabia.
sentences.zh: 外交关系。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: For President Biden, the idea of getting such a huge diplomatic breakthrough was worth taking a bit more nuclear risk.
sentences.zh: 对拜登总统来说，取得如此巨大的外交突破值得承担多一点的核风险。

sentences.en: For President Trump, the idea of getting a big business deal is worth taking a little more nuclear risk.
sentences.zh: 对特朗普总统来说，达成一项巨额商业交易值得承担多一点的核风险。

sentences.en: I want to talk a little bit more about the timing of all of this, David, because obviously this deal is coming in the middle of the United States war with Iran, right?
sentences.zh: 大卫，我想多聊聊这一切的时间节点，很明显，这项协议正值美国与伊朗战争期间，对吧？

sentences.en: And we know that there has been tension between Saudi Arabia and the United States over the war to the point where I think at one point
sentences.zh: 我们知道沙特阿拉伯和美国之间因这场战争一直存在紧张关系，以至于我认为在某个时刻

sentences.en: Saudi Arabia closed its airspace to the United States for the military for a period of time.
sentences.zh: 沙特阿拉伯一度对美国军方关闭了其领空。

sentences.en: So can you just talk a little bit about whether the war has anything to do with why we're seeing this happen now?
sentences.zh: 所以你能谈谈这场战争是否与我们现在看到这一幕的发生有任何关系吗？

sentences.en: Well, certainly, as we've discussed, this was long brewing.
sentences.zh: 当然，正如我们所讨论的，这酝酿已久。

sentences.en: So there was some thinking, in fact, that the deal would be signed back in February.
sentences.zh: 因此，事实上曾有人认为该协议早在2月份就会签署。

sentences.en: But then the war broke out with Iran and the Saudis were angry at Washington for several reasons.
sentences.zh: 但随后与伊朗的战争爆发了，沙特人对华盛顿感到不满，原因有几个。

sentences.en: I remember having dinner with a very senior
sentences.zh: 我记得我和一位高级别的

sentences.en: Saudi official just hours before
sentences.zh: 沙特官员共进晚餐，就在几小时前

sentences.en: President Trump ordered the first bombs dropped on Tehran in February.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统于2月份下令向德黑兰投下第一批炸弹。

sentences.en: And that official did not have much notice, if any, that the war was about to break out.
sentences.zh: 那位官员几乎没有得到什么通知（如果有的话），得知战争即将爆发。

sentences.en: Then the Iranians took everybody by surprise by actually expanding the war to the Gulf allies and particularly hitting American bases.
sentences.zh: 然后伊朗人让所有人大吃一惊，他们实际上将战争扩大到了海湾盟国，特别是袭击了美军基地。

sentences.en: And again, there was a lot of tension about whether the United States was putting enough effort into protecting
sentences.zh: 同样，关于美国是否付出足够努力来保护

sentences.en: Saudi airspace from these incoming missiles and drones.
